title: RAW UNREVIEWED: value-one source letters force single-sign additive packets on a matched complete message
summary: A source-conditioned necessary consequence of the historical additive letter-packet idea: when every counted whole output group represents exactly one source letter by a sum of strictly positive integer working-sign weights, every source letter of value1 must produce a one-sign group. The elementary lemma is already present in959; the distinct proposed endpoint is a matched-denominator source-to-output singleton-frequency floor, independent of packet-choice policy and alphabet renaming. No source, native count, fitted value or experiment is selected. A secondary identical-group triple consequence is retained unassessed.
ownership: Root proposed the frequency endpoint and the later triple side consequence. The bounded producer checked the proof, prior scopes and denominator obligations, without data measurement or claiming an independent discovery.

design.mechanism: Retain959's letterwise additive channel as a conditional model. A source letter has a publicly fixed positive integer target value. Exactly one complete counted output group carries that value as the sum of its nonempty sequence of counted working signs, each with strictly positive integer weight. Alternatives for the same sum may be chosen by any predeclared human policy; this necessary bound does not require fitting or inventing that policy.
design.unit: A complete explicitly delimited source-letter sequence and the corresponding complete sequence of ordinary output packet groups. One source letter equals exactly one whole counted packet; any source spaces, punctuation, controls, paragraphs or physical line continuations need an explicit separate contract before comparison.
design.prediction: If N source letters include K letters whose target value is1, at least K of the N corresponding ordinary packet groups contain exactly one counted working sign. Thus the singleton share among those ordinary groups is at least K/N. Other source-letter values may also use one-sign packets, so this is a lower bound, not an equality.
design.proof: For a packet of length L>=1 with positive integer weights w1,...,wL, the sum is at least L. If its target sum is1, then L<=1, hence L=1 and the sole weight is1. No choice among equal-sum packets, homophonic weight assignments or global sign renaming changes this length obligation. If the allowed output inventory has no weight1 sign, any occurrence of a value1 source letter is unrepresentable instead.
design.contrast: 1231and1232ask whether selected whole written groups can receive allowed sums under an unknown assignment. They do not require any specified source letter to occur or compare a complete source's value1 frequency to whole-output length1 frequency. This proposal adds that source-content obligation; it is not a larger-panel rerun of their arithmetic fit and does not revive1232's distinct-value contract.
design.distinct_from_the_fixed_22_codeword_defe: One source letter may have many different positive-sum packets. Even22source letters therefore do not limit the number of permitted physical packet codewords to22. The new fixed-at-most22-codeword defect consequence does not exclude this alias-rich additive contract. The value1 singleton obligation nevertheless holds for every legal packet individually. No packet-count restriction is silently added here.
design.smallest_falsifier: Only after a complete source/control message and matching packet denominator are prospectively specified: fewer singleton ordinary output groups than the number of required value1 source letters contradicts that exact source-plus-framing-plus-positive-sum writer, without a sign-key fit. If the two texts are merely unrelated language samples, any result is a fixed-source control result rather than a logical contradiction of the manuscript's unknown language.
design.positive_ceiling: Meeting the floor only leaves this necessary consequence unrefuted. It supplies no working-sign value, letter assignment, language identification, packet-choice policy, framing proof, historical attribution or whole-message inverse.
design.human_purpose_and_cost: The historical purpose is arithmetic concealment of ordinary correspondence. A scribe learns the numeric alphabet, chooses legal sums and writes packets; a reader learns the same table and sums them. Source literacy, actual packet/source-word boundaries, unsupported characters, punctuation, physical continuation and a usable choice policy are paid costs still missing from the historical toy example. This RAW is a falsification proposal, not a newly completed writer.

historical_scope.original_locator: al-Qalqashandi, Subh al-Asha IX, printed232 bottom–233 top in the retained1916Cairo edition; the passage reports Ibn al-Durayhim. Existing raw source receipt and earlier image inspection are relied upon; no image or external source is opened here.
historical_scope.already_present_lemma: 959 human_rule_and_cost.writing_length already states that a positive additive value1 realization cannot contain two positive terms. This card does not present that arithmetic observation as new.
historical_scope.source_letter_not_in_example: The demonstrated source word supplies a letterwise packet example, not a complete text containing and counting every source-letter value. The value1 obligation uses the separately declared complete numeric alphabet and the prospectively supplied source content; it is not a frequency observed in the four-packet example.
historical_scope.framing_limit: The example visually separates the source letters of one word. It does not demonstrate both source-word boundaries and letter-packet boundaries in a multiword message. The later separator prescription concerns a different cipher subsection and cannot silently supply this missing two-level contract.
historical_scope.alphabet_limit: 22working signs, stable positive integer weights and one written group per source letter remain reconstruction assumptions. The historical letter inventory and its numeric table are not an identified native alphabet. No native letter is named alif here.

denominator_and_selection_obligations: Do not compare K/N for a complete source against an old native strict-interior subset without a prospective mapping or valid censoring bound. Value1 letters could disproportionately occur at omitted line/group edges.

If exactly r of the N corresponding source-letter packets are omitted by a known selection, only max(0,K-r) singleton groups are unconditionally forced among the retained N-r groups. This conservative arithmetic requires that r actually bounds removed corresponding letter packets, not an unrelated sample size.

The old manual packet was selected to show frequent, rare and long forms and then filtered by definite interior seams. It is not a random or complete frequency sample. Equal-looking filtering labels alone do not make its singleton fraction comparable to a whole source.

If C extra control groups are inserted, the letter-packet count still forces at least K singleton letter packets, but the fraction among all N+C groups has only the floor K/(N+C). C and the control treatment must be fixed and paid; an unspecified number of controls can arbitrarily dilute the ratio.

If a control is added inside each printed group but excluded from its arithmetic value, one counted complete group need no longer be a pure packet. That is a different premise, not an exception erased from the denominator.

Source-word boundaries, punctuation, names, diacritics and unsupported source signs must be retained through an explicit channel or removed by an explicitly stated projection before selecting the endpoint. They cannot be discarded after observing a failure.

No fixed natural language, complete source text, native reference panel, tolerance or statistical decision rule is selected in this RAW. Without such a source commitment, the unknown plaintext may simply contain a different number of value1 letters, so no manuscript-wide frequency claim follows.
Alternate transcriptions must remain separate readings of one manuscript, not pooled independent samples. All inherited scope and reserved-material restrictions remain.
contract_changes_outside_the_bound: Zero-valued null signs can pad a value1 packet; strict positivity is essential.
Negative weights, subtraction, modulo arithmetic or noninteger positive weights invalidate the stated length proof.
Several source letters per written group, a source letter split across groups, uncounted internal control signs or overlapping/contextual physical realization alter the group/length contract.
A source projection that deletes or changes particular letters is a different source contract and must be declared before any comparison.
A different output unit analysis can change what one sign means; the lemma alone does not identify native atoms.

unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.extra_premises: The output working-sign weights are fixed across occurrences and each permissible target value names exactly one source-letter unit. Every group in the triple is an ordinary single-letter packet, with source order preserved and no inserted control group mistaken for a packet.
unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.lemma: Three identical complete output groups have the same sum, hence the same decoded source-letter value, hence three equal consecutive source-letter units. This holds even when one source letter has many permitted alternative packets.
unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.nonconverse: Three equal consecutive source letters need not produce three identical groups, because different permitted packets may be chosen. No source repetition is demanded merely because equal-sum aliases exist.
unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.boundary_limit: Consecutive means in the explicitly encoded source-letter stream. A triple may cross a source-word boundary if that boundary has been deliberately projected away or written in a separate preserved channel; it is not automatically three letters within one source word. Punctuation or boundary controls that interrupt visible adjacency must be modeled explicitly.
unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.pointer_caution: 857is cited only as the parent-supplied existing triple-obligation family. This producer did not reopen its native rows or recheck exact counts/locations in this block. Existing triples alone do not choose or refute a source text.
unassessed_secondary_identical_triple_co.limit: Noninjective source-letter values or context-dependent decoding can let equal sums denote different source letters and would change this side lemma. No native repeated group is assigned a letter or meaning.
